html:
"Lombard duchies" is the map's label, for 800 and 900, for the Lombard states of southern Italy, centred on Benevento, Salerno and Capua.

When Charlemagne conquered the Lombard kingdom in the north in 774, the Duchy of Benevento in the south stayed free. Its duke Arechis II took the title of prince and paid the Franks only loose respect. The older Lombard duchies were its roots.

In 849 a civil war split it into the principalities of Benevento and Salerno, and Capua later broke off as well. The Lombard princes lived amid stronger powers: the Carolingians, the Byzantines on the coasts, the Papal States, and Arab raiders from Africa and Sicily, who at one point held Bari. In the 1000s Norman adventurers took service with them and then took over; Salerno fell to Robert Guiscard in 1077.
sum: "Lombard duchies" is the map's label, for 800 and 900, for the Lombard states of southern Italy, centred on Benevento, Salerno and Capua.
